I need to make a decision for the Monopoly game.

I have $3,216 and three hotels on my properties. Player 1 has only $34 and is heavily mortgaged, though they do own several buildings. I am considering whether to trade or take another action.

I will keep both get-out-of-jail cards and avoid selling hotels or unmortgaging the railroads. Player 1 is on Short Line, so I am checking the board order around that space.

Player 1's next rolls from Short Line will hit their own properties or tax spaces. They cannot reach my pink set.

The maximum roll from Short Line is 12 spaces, so Player 1 cannot reach my pink properties on their next turn. I am now weighing whether to take any post-turn action, specifically noting that unmortgaging the railroads would cost $110 and $99 respectively, though Player 1 already owns all other railroads.

Unmortgaging the railroads is not worthwhile. Player 1 already owns St. James and New York, so trading Tennessee would complete their orange monopoly. I should avoid giving them cash or that property. Their Park Place and Boardwalk are dangerous if I land on them.

I am calculating exact rent values to assess the danger. Park Place with four houses pays $1,300 and Boardwalk with three houses pays $1,400. My cash of $3,216 covers both. I am also reviewing the light blue properties: Connecticut hotel is $600, while Oriental and Vermont hotels are $550 each.

I am considering trading cash for Boardwalk or Park Place to neutralize the threat. Player 1 would gain cash to survive my pink hotels, but they would lose their main weapon. They still own Park Place, so that danger remains.

I have decided against trading cash for Boardwalk or Park Place. That would give Player 1 the money they need to survive my pink hotels and could let them land on them again. Selling a hotel would also reduce rent and help them survive. I will keep both get-out-of-jail cards and do nothing.
